project.name: snappea-wasm
project.description: SnapPea kernel + PARI/GMP compiled to WebAssembly via Emscripten. Computation-only npm package — no UI, no rendering. Embeddable in Pyodide, Node.js, or any browser JS runtime.

goals: Ship the SnapPea C kernel as a single statically-linked WASM module via npm
Include PARI/GP + GMP for exact arithmetic (Smith normal form, homology)
Zero UI dependencies — computation only, consumers supply their own frontend
Usable from plain JS/TS, Node.js, Pyodide, Deno, or any WASM host
All existing SnapPy kernel-level tests pass against the WASM build
GitHub Actions CI: build, test, publish to npm
non_goals: No GUI, Tkinter, OpenGL, or rendering of any kind
No Python runtime bundled (consumers bring their own, e.g. Pyodide)
No Cython — replaced by JS/TS bindings via Emscripten ccall/cwrap
No census databases bundled (load on demand via fetch or user-supplied data)
No SnapPyHP quad-double precision in v1 (future enhancement)

architecture.linking: Static — single .wasm binary containing SnapPea kernel + PARI + GMP
architecture.rationale: Static linking avoids dynamic linking overhead (5-10% perf hit) and simplifies distribution as a single npm package.

source_components.name: PARI/GP
source_components.purpose: Smith normal form (matsnf), exact integer matrix ops, number-theoretic functions
source_components.pari_build_patch: #undef UNIX appended to paricfg.h (prevents getpwuid/popen calls)

source_components.name: GMP
source_components.purpose: Arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic used by PARI
source_components.note: Included via wasm-pari-gmp build or compiled separately with Emscripten

output_artifacts.index.js: Main entry — async init, typed API wrapper

exported_api.description: JS/TS API surface exposed via Emscripten EXPORTED_FUNCTIONS + cwrap/ccall wrappers. Grouped by domain.

core_lifecycle.init: async () => Module — load WASM, initialize PARI stack

cusps.set_cusp_info: (tri: TriangulationPtr, cuspIndex: number, m: number, l: number) => void
cusps.get_holonomy: (tri: TriangulationPtr, cuspIndex: number) => { meridian: Complex, longitude: Complex }

pari_direct.note: Thin wrapper over gp_embedded for direct PARI/GP access

types.CuspInfo: { topology: 'torus' | 'Klein_bottle', m: number, l: number, modulus: Complex, shape: Complex }
types.GroupPresentation: { num_generators: number, relations: string[], num_orig_gens: number }
types.GeodesicInfo: { length: Complex, parity: number, topology: number }
types.SymmetryGroup: { order: number, is_amphicheiral: boolean, is_invertible: boolean }

file_io.problem: kernel/kernel_code/interface.c uses stdio FILE* for SnapPea file format I/O
file_io.solution: Replace with Emscripten MEMFS virtual filesystem + string-based triangulation_from_string / triangulation_to_string wrappers

memory_management.solution: Works as-is under Emscripten. Set ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH=1, INITIAL_MEMORY=64MB

random_number_generation.problem: Uses rand() from stdlib in simplify_triangulation.c
random_number_generation.solution: Emscripten provides rand() implementation. Seed via JavaScript if reproducibility needed.

long_computation_callback.problem: uLongComputationContinues() callback pattern for UI responsiveness
long_computation_callback.solution: Provide no-op stub, or allow JS callback registration for cancellation support

unix_kit.solution: Stub or remove — console I/O and signal handling not needed in WASM

build_system.note: Following wasm-pari-gmp convention: shell scripts for each build stage (build-gmp.sh, build-pari.sh, build-snappea.sh, link.sh)

src/.snappea/: Vendored SnapPea kernel source (kernel_code/, addl_code/, headers/)
src/.pari/: PARI source or pre-built WASM artifact from wasm-pari-gmp
src/.gmp/: GMP source or pre-built WASM artifact
src/.bindings/: C wrapper functions for Emscripten EXPORTED_FUNCTIONS

test/.unit/: C-level unit tests compiled to WASM and run via Node.js
test/.integration/: JS/TS tests exercising the public API
test/.fixtures/: SnapPea triangulation files (.tri) for test input
test/.reference/: Expected outputs from native SnapPy for comparison

scripts/.extract-fixtures.py: Pull test triangulations from SnapPy census
scripts/.generate-reference.py: Run native SnapPy to produce expected test outputs

memory_strategy.note: wasm-pari-gmp uses fixed INITIAL_MEMORY=2146435072 (~2GB) with NO memory growth for PARI performance. For snappea-wasm we have two options.

option_a.name: Fixed 2GB (match wasm-pari-gmp)
option_a.cons: Wastes memory if only doing simple triangulations, may fail on 32-bit browsers

option_b.name: Growable from 64MB
option_b.cons: Slight PARI performance impact (acceptable per Emscripten WASM docs — the asm.js perf issue does not apply to WASM)

memory_strategy.recommendation: Option B for v1. Most consumers will do small computations. Add configurable initial memory in init() options.

build_system.build_scripts_note: Following wasm-pari-gmp convention: shell scripts (build-gmp.sh, build-pari.sh, build-snappea.sh), NOT Makefile
build_steps: 1. scripts/build-gmp.sh — Download GMP 6.2.1, emconfigure/emmake, install to build/local/
2. scripts/build-pari.sh — Download PARI 2.13.2, patch paricfg.h (#undef UNIX), emconfigure/emmake with GMP paths
3. scripts/build-snappea.sh — Compile SnapPea kernel_code + addl_code + stubs with emcc -c, produce .o files
4. scripts/build-bindings.sh — Compile C binding wrappers (src/bindings/) with emcc -c
5. scripts/link.sh — Final emcc link: all .o files + libpari.a + libgmp.a → dist/snappea_kernel.{wasm,js}
6. scripts/gen-types.sh — Generate index.d.ts from binding signatures
7. scripts/package.sh — Bundle into dist/ with package.json, README, LICENSE

prior_art.jsage: https://github.com/sagemathinc/JSage — Package architecture for WASM math libraries, each in packages/<name>/dist/wasm/

testing.framework: vitest (JS/TS) + custom C harness compiled to WASM

test_tiers.description: WASM loads, PARI initializes, basic triangulation round-trips
Each exported function called with known inputs, output compared to reference values from native SnapPy
Homology, fundamental group, symmetry group for census manifolds
Canonize, isometry detection, length spectrum, link complement triangulation
pari_eval and smith_normal_form with various matrix inputs
SnapPy doctest-derived fixtures: run same inputs, compare outputs to native SnapPy reference values

reference_generation.method: Run native SnapPy (CPython) on test inputs, serialize outputs as JSON fixtures
manifolds: m003 (sister of figure-eight — hyperbolic, H₁ = Z/5 + Z)
reference_generation.output_format: JSON: { manifold, volume, solution_type, num_tet, cusps, homology, chern_simons, fundamental_group, symmetry_group }

steps: Cache Emscripten sysroot + GMP/PARI WASM objects
bash scripts/build-gmp.sh && bash scripts/build-pari.sh && bash scripts/build-snappea.sh && bash scripts/link.sh

caching.emscripten_cache: ~/.emscripten_cache — sysroot and system library WASM objects

npm_package.name: @snappea/kernel
npm_package.usage_example_pyodide:
import asyncio
from js import snappea_kernel  # Loaded globally via <script> tag

async def main():
    snappea = await snappea_kernel.init()
    tri = snappea.triangulationFromString(data)
    print(snappea.volume(tri))
    snappea.freeTriangulation(tri)

asyncio.ensure_future(main())

wasm_limitations: No signal handling — Ctrl+C during computation kills Node.js (WASM has no signals). Provide cancellation via uLongComputationContinues callback.
No threads — single-threaded only (no -pthread). Long computations block the caller.
32-bit WASM — limited to ~4 GB address space maximum.
No filesystem by default — PARI commands requiring data files (e.g. polgalois) need --embed-file at build time. SnapPea file I/O uses MEMFS.
No popen/getpwuid — #undef UNIX patch required for PARI build.

risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Use pre-built WASM artifacts from sagemathinc/wasm-pari-gmp. Fall back to building from their Makefile.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: SnapPea kernel assumes IEEE 754 double edge cases
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: WASM mandates IEEE 754. Run T5 regression suite to catch discrepancies.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Memory growth performance in tight loops
risks_and_mitigations.impact: Low — WASM ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH is efficient unlike asm.js
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Set generous INITIAL_MEMORY (64MB). Profile with census batch test.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: WASM binary size too large for casual browser use
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Target <4MB. Use -O3 + wasm-opt. Offer gzipped variant (~1MB). Consider lazy PARI loading if size exceeds 5MB.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: License compatibility (SnapPea GPL-2 + PARI GPL-2 + GMP LGPL)
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Ship as GPL-2.0-or-later. Document license provenance in NOTICE file.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: No C-level unit tests exist upstream
risks_and_mitigations.impact: Medium — must create test harness from scratch
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Generate reference fixtures from native SnapPy. Compare WASM outputs to reference JSON.
